strings.name: Diego Della Valle
strings.summary: Diego Della Valle is an Italian entrepreneur who joined the family shoemaking business in 1975 and helped expand its brands and international operations. He has long been involved in managing Tod’s Group, while he and his family have also participated in football investment and heritage restoration funding.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026. Chairman and CEO are distinguished: Galantic became CEO in 2024 and left at the end of April 2026. A November report again calls Della Valle chairman and CEO, but the effective date of reappointment has not been verified.
strings.influence.rationale: Developed Italian brands including Tod’s, participating in premium manufacturing, luxury management and heritage restoration funding.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education and honorary degrees
strings.facts.f1.value: Studied law in Bologna; the economics and management-related degrees awarded by Ancona in 2000 and Sannio in 2017 were honorary, not earned qualifications.
strings.facts.f2.label: Family and management
strings.facts.f2.value: Participates in the family business with his younger brother Andrea; chairman, CEO and vice chairman are separate roles, and family assets are not necessarily his sole personal property.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Heritage funding
strings.highlights.h1.text: Italy’s culture authorities recorded €25 million in funding from Tod’s Group for Colosseum restoration; this was corporate support for a public-authority project, not restoration carried out by him alone.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Calciopoli case record
strings.highlights.h2.text: Reporting in 2015 states that the Court of Cassation rejected his and Andrea’s appeals, with the offences already extinguished by limitation; a time bar is not an acquittal on the merits.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Responds to creative director’s departure
strings.timeline.t1.text: Vogue reported his thanks to Matteo Tamburini in a company statement; this management statement does not mean he took over the design work himself.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Galantic takes over as CEO
strings.timeline.t2.text: Reuters reported John Galantic’s appointment as CEO, with Della Valle retaining the chairmanship.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Tod’s delisting takes effect
strings.timeline.t3.text: Exchange records confirm delisting after Crown Bidco’s tender offer; June 5–6 was the preceding trading suspension.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Family sells Fiorentina
strings.timeline.t4.text: Rocco Commisso bought the club from the Della Valle brothers; this does not establish that the criminal case directly caused the sale.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Calciopoli appeal outcome reported
strings.timeline.t5.text: Sky reported that the Court of Cassation rejected the brothers’ appeals and noted that limitation had already applied at the appeal stage.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Takes management roles at Tod’s Group
strings.timeline.t6.text: His biography records appointment as chairman and managing director; this historical starting point does not imply uninterrupted service as CEO to the present.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Receives Knight of Labour honour
strings.timeline.t7.text: Italy’s presidency records his award of Cavaliere del Lavoro for contributions to business.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joins family shoemaking business
strings.timeline.t8.text: After studying law and working in the United States, he helped his father manage the business and learned high-quality production techniques.
